data.content:
## Build Failure Analysis

**Solution:** `BuildDiag.sln` — 3 projects: `Core`, `Services`, `Api`
**Dependency chain:** `Core` ← `Services` ← `Api` (Api also references Core directly)

---

### Root Cause (1 issue, 3 errors)

**Project: `Services.csproj`** — `UserService.cs` uses `Newtonsoft.Json` but the package is **not referenced** in the project file.

| Error | Location | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| CS0246 | `UserService.cs(2,7)` | `using Newtonsoft.Json;` — namespace not found |
| CS0246 | `UserService.cs(3,7)` | `using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq;` — namespace not found |
| CS0246 | `UserService.cs(22,19)` | `JObject` type not found (follows from above) |

### Cascading Failure

**Project: `Api.csproj`** — never compiled. It depends on `Services` via `<ProjectReference>`, so when Services failed at `CoreCompile`, Api stopped at `ResolveProjectReferences` and was never built. **No independent errors in Api.**

**Project: `Core.csproj`** — built successfully (no errors).

---

### Fix

Add the missing NuGet package reference to `Services/Services.csproj`:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Or run:
```
dotnet add Services/Services.csproj package Newtonsoft.Json
```

This single fix resolves all 3 compiler errors and unblocks the Api project build.
